top.title: Crime pays: how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus
top.description: Ever since it crashed on to PC and consoles in the late 90s, GTA has been tearing up the game-making rulebook. We explore how its cultural references, rebel spirit and sprawling sense of freedom make it a definitive work of art In the 00s, when the Grand Theft Auto developer Rockstar Games revealed a new project, video game writers from all over the UK would make the journey to the company’s office in London. They would be ushered one by one into a darkened room to sit facing an enormous TV. There would be a dish of sweets on a low bench in front of them but, in the reverential hush that descended, it was never entirely clear if it was acceptable to eat them. After a few moments, the screen would come to life. Rockstar would sometimes begin its presentation not with footage from its new game, but clips from classic movies. This is the context of what we are making, Rockstar was saying, and that is where we belong. Continue reading...

top.title: This Vikings QB timeline since 2023 proves Kevin O’Connell isn’t the guru everybody thought
top.description: This Vikings QB timeline since 2023 proves Kevin O’Connell isn’t the guru everybody thought originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is one of the winningest active coaches in the NFL, but his status as a quarterback whisperer is being called into question. At one point, O'Connell was considered a bright young head coach who would get the most out of any quarterback on his team. Over time, though, the Vikings still haven't solved their quarterback issues, while Minnesota's former signal-callers have thrived elsewhere. Now, with Kyler Murray the latest Vikings quarterback who isn't playing up to expectations, O'Connell's status as a quarterback guru has waned. The Vikings head coach needs to turn that around for Minnesota to compete for a Super Bowl. Here's a breakdown of every quarterback to start a game with the Vikings under O'Connell. MORE : Who needs Jonathan Taylor the most? Vikings QB timeline under Kevin O'Connell Kirk Cousins (2022-23) O'Connell inherited Cousins when he first arrived in Minnesota in 2022, and the two were a great pair. Cousins started every game for the Vikings that year, leading Minnesota to the playoffs with a 13-4 record while totaling 4,547 passing yards and 29 passing touchdowns. That season continued Cousins' strong play for the Vikings, as his numbers were similar to his seasonal production since signing with Minnesota in 2018. From a wins standpoint, though, Cousins had only won double-digit games once before and had never won more than 10 contests. In 2023, Cousins had a solid start before he tore his Achilles, which was a huge blow ahead of free agency. In 25 games with O'Connell, Cousins produced 275.12 passing yards per game with 37 passing touchdowns in total. Josh Dobbs (2023) After Cousins tore his Achilles, the Vikings traded for quarterback Josh Dobbs, who had been solid for the Arizona Cardinals in place of an injured Kyler Murray. While the Cardinals had just one win up to that point, Dobbs had 14 total touchdowns, passing and rushing, and showed enough to get a chance elsewhere. Dobbs' production slightly dipped when he began playing for the Vikings, and he was unable to fill Cousins' shoes. Dobbs started four games for Minnesota, appearing in five total contests, and had just 179 passing yards per game. In the final five games of the season, Mullens started three of them but failed to lead the team to a win in any of those starts. top.title: 4 winners and losers from the Patriots’ loss to the Packers
top.description: The New England Patriots were largely uncompetitive in a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-4 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 9 contest. Winners N/A Losers CB Christian Gonzalez: The Patriots’ top corner was not his usual self on Sunday. Gonzalez was on scene for several explosive plays and took fault for a miscommunication that resulted in Matthew Golden’s 5-yard touchdown. Both Golden and Christian Watson posted 80-plus yards with Gonzalez in coverage while he surrendered 187 yards on a career-high 10 receptions in total. New England’s secondary is too talented to be playing at this level in recent weeks, and that begins with Gonzalez. QB Drake Maye: There were positive moments for Maye against Green Bay, but the quarterback ultimately struggled throwing three first-half interceptions that led to an early deficit. Maye’s interceptions came when he pushed the ball down the field, which was a concern entering the week against a zone heavy Packers defense that led the league in takeaways. Offensive line: Behind their fifth different starting combination, the pressure got to Maye early on Sunday. The Packers’ pressure schemes gave New England’s front fits as Maye was sacked four times and was forced into four throwaways. In total, Maye was under pressure on over 50% of his drop backs. RG Matt Pryor was initially charted with four pressures to lead the group. Injuries: As they have all season, the injuries continued to pile up. The Patriots lost CB Carlton Davis (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee), ST Brenden Schooler (hamstring), and RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) in the loss. They did get positive news with starting left tackle Will Campbell, who would have returned in a closer game, but the roster is beaten down ahead of a trip to Germany — which could alter recovery timelines as the team departs Wednesday evening. Honorable mentions DeMario Douglas recorded his second career 100-yard game behind a beautifully-ran 36-yard corner-post route. Mack Hollins finished with three catches and a touchdown in his return. Efton Chism also found the end zone and had five catches. It was a down day for Kyle Williams, who failed to haul in a deep ball and was targeted on Maye’s second interception (which was on the quarterback). Rhamondre Stevenson’s fumble was the Patriots fourth turnover of the day. They now have a -11 turnover differential on the season. Milton Williams flashed throughout the day with three pressures and a TFL in the run game. Rookie cornerback Karon Prunty replaced an injured Carlton Davis at corner. While Prunty had an impressive gunner rep to help down a punt, the Packers immediately picked on him defensively. Packers were 4-of-5 in the red zone. The Patriots kickoff coverage continues to be shaky as they allowed a 48-yard return. Punter Mitch Wishnowsky continues to punt well and recorded four i20s.

nigeria.title: FG Sets December For Kaduna-Kano Rail Project Inauguration
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu is accelerating the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria, with the Kaduna–Kano Standard Gauge Railway scheduled for inauguration on December 3, 2026. A statement by Dele Alake, Spokesperson, APC Presidential Campaign Council, noted that the 203-kilometre Kaduna–Zaria–Kano railway project, one of the administration’s legacy projects, has reached approximately 90 per cent completion, while the 400-kilometre Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway project has attained 70 per cent completion. Kaduna-Kano Rail Project. The Federal Government says the project is 70 per cent completed. “When President Tinubu assumed office in 2023, Kano-Kastina-Maradi rail project was at barely 5% while Kaduna-Kano was less than 30% complete. “The projects demonstrate the administration’s commitment to expanding Nigeria’s railway infrastructure, improving regional connectivity and facilitating the movement of passengers and goods across the country and beyond”. Alake noted, saying that the project, an extension of the existing Abuja–Kaduna standard gauge line, will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano, strengthening transportation links across major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria. The two rail projects were recently inspected on the directive of President Tinubu by a Federal Government team led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi, who expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation. The inspection included a train test-run journey from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano, allowing officials to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort. Alake noted that the President has also directed that all outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis should be resolved immediately so that the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano will be completed. The completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section out of the entire 205-kilometre stretch of the Kaduna-Kano rail project and the 250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Kastina section of the Kano-Maradi project will be inaugurated by December 3, 2026. According to him, when operational, the Kaduna–Kano railway will improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors. Similarly, the Kano–Katsina–Maradi railway, which has reached 70 percent completion, is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and the neighbouring Niger Republic. Alake added that in line with President Tinubu’s agenda, all ongoing infrastructure projects will be delivered in every part of the country as scheduled. nigeria.title: African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United
nigeria.description: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson scored after just four minutes for Aston Villa, who twice surrendered two-goal leads in a remarkable 4-4 Premier League draw away to Manchester United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put his side 2-0 ahead against United, but it wasn’t enough to inspire a victory at Old Trafford. When Jackson tapped in after United goalkeeper Senne Lammens palmed the ball into his path, it appeared the 25-year-old’s ninth goal in 14 games in all competitions this term would be the spark for a comfortable Villa win. But in an incredible finale, United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue a draw. YANN GBOHO (Coventry City) The Ivory Coast winger scored his first Premier League goal in a 3-1 defeat at Everton. Gboho, signed from French side Toulouse in September, put Coventry ahead with a composed finish after evading slack defending in the 52nd minute. But Frank Lampard’s team crumbled after the 25-year-old’s strike as Everton scored three times to leave the visitors one point above the relegation zone. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri continued his superb season with another goal to help Santander win 2-1 at Malaga. The 21-year-old bagged his ninth of the campaign with a simple finish to tuck a rebound home into the empty net. Only Raphinha, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal have scored more goals this season in La Liga. ITALY KONAN N’DRI (Lecce) After Angolan Kailonda Gaspar conceded a 60th-minute own goal to give Torino the lead in a clash of bottom-half Serie A clubs, Niger international N’Dri scored to salvage a 1-1 draw for visiting Lecce. The architect of the equaliser was Mali international Lassana Coulibaly. GERMANY EZECHIEL BANZUZI (RB Leipzig) Banzuzi’s goal proved the turning point as he kick-started Leipzig’s recovery to beat Augsburg 5-2 at home in the Bundesliga after conceding inside the opening minute. Anton Kade had Augsburg in front after 36 seconds but Banzuzi levelled in the 33rd minute when he turned a Brajan Gruda pass into the bottom right corner. The 21-year-old Democratic Republic of Congo internnational has two goals and two assists in the league this season. UCHENNA OGUNDU (Augsburg) Ogundu’s first goal in Augsburg colours was a mere consolation as his side crashed at Leipzig. With Leipzig 5-1 up, Augsburg’s Alexis Claude Maurice intercepted the ball and sent his side in the other direction. Fabian Rieder latched on to Claude Maurice’s pass before finding Ogundu, who slid the ball into the bottom corner. FRANCE LASSINE SINAYOKO (Paris FC) Ligue 1’s leading scorer Sinayoko netted after 63 minutes to give third-placed Paris FC a 1-0 win at lowly Auxerre. nigeria.title: Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday. Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections. The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.” “I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday. The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed. “For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television. “We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added. – ‘They had enough’ – Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat. Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.” “Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.” In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms. “They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.” Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September. Iranian state television said the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked overnight Sunday, hours after the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions there. Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war. Outright fighting has largely subsided, but Iran continues in its efforts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global energy supplies, while the US Navy maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. nigeria.title: Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?
nigeria.description: Tech executive Alice Huang is the woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, according to media reports. Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International. Here is what we know about her and the company: – Who is Alice Huang? – Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia boss, according to the New York Times, which first reported that Jensen Huang was the alleged target of a spy plot. Despite their shared surname, Alice Huang is no relation to the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born head of the world’s most valuable company. The Times, citing people briefed on the surveillance, said that Alice Huang speaks good English and is well connected at the highest level of the global AI chip industry. The sector is highly sensitive as the United States and China race to develop advanced AI systems with potential military applications. An online search brought up a short profile for Alice Huang, with her photo, on a Chinese fund database. It listed previous jobs including at HSBC bank, and as a reporter for Chinese media outlets CCTV and Hunan TV. AFP was unable to verify the contents of the profile, or who had written it, but has attempted to contact the companies cited. – How are the pair connected? – Media reports last week said they had a close relationship, and Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on Sunday he was “deeply sorry” for being “unfaithful to my wife”. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. Alice Huang is also seen following the Nvidia chief as he re-enters the restaurant after talking to journalists outside, running her fingers down his lower back. They later leave the restaurant in the same car. – What is Megaspeed? – US officials concluded last year that Alice Huang was targeting Jensen Huang as a spy, according to the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal. nigeria.title: Gunmen kill security operative, three others in Plateau attack
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three residents and a security operative during an attack on Bel village in Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, while several other persons sustained injuries. The attack reportedly occurred at about 9 p.m. on Sunday when the gunmen stormed the community and opened fire on residents. A resident of the community, Mr Bulus Bot, who confirmed the incident, said the attackers invaded the village at night and shot indiscriminately at innocent citizens. “The gunmen stormed the community at about 9 p.m. and opened fire on innocent citizens, leaving some people dead and others injured,” he said. Bot described the incident as a disturbing attack on the community, noting that residents were caught up in the violence when the gunmen opened fire. He said some persons sustained injuries during the attack, adding to the concern among residents over the safety of people in the area. The Publicity Secretary of Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the killings and identified three of the victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. He alleged that a soldier was also among those killed in the attack, bringing the reported death toll to four. Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, and called on security operatives to track down those responsible. He urged security agencies to ensure that the perpetrators were identified and brought to justice, stressing the need for decisive action to prevent further attacks on communities in the area. Efforts to get a reaction from security operatives on the attack were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Billionaire businessman Tony Elumelu has credited his mother with teaching him the fundamentals of business, using her experience as a small restaurant owner to emphasise the importance of women’s economic leadership and participation in Africa’s development. Elumelu said his earliest lessons in entrepreneurship, including risk management, cash flow, customer relations, discipline and resilience, came from watching his mother build a business and provide for her family. Elumelu, who spoke on Friday at the 25th Annual Conference of Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ), held at Eko Hotel and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos, recalled how his mother’s hard work shaped his understanding of business. “I did not start with capital. I started with a mother, a mother who ran a small restaurant and worked harder than anyone I’ve ever known. “I watched her turn very little into a living, and a living into a future for our children. That was my first business school,” he said. He added that his understanding of the practical demands of running a business came from observing her daily experiences. “My first lesson in risk, in cash flow, in customers, in discipline, in hard work, in resilience, in getting up the next morning when the day before had gone very badly, came all from her, a woman,” he said. nigeria.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it had opened a probe into chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing. The executive, also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said. In a message to company employees released Sunday, the Nvidia chief acknowledged having an affair and apologized to his family and company staff. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Jensen Huang is a huge figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race. The Times said Alice Huang’s relationship with the Nvidia chief could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump’s planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China. Asked whether the Nvidia chief would be joining the president’s trip to Asia, which includes the Asia-Pacific summit in China’s Shenzhen on Sunday, Trump told reporters: “I don’t know but I’ll certainly take him.” Trump said Huang was “a fine person, but you never know what’s going on. I’m sure — I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” – ‘Speculation’ – Nvidia said in a statement it had opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The statement added: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as “groundless speculation.” China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips. Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies. Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter. nigeria.description: The death toll from Saudi strikes on Yemen’s Sanaa province climbed to 44, including more than 20 children, the Houthis said on their television channel Monday. A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen’s long-running conflict fell apart in July, restarting fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government. Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites. “The toll from the Saudi enemy’s massacre in the Alshariyah area of Bani Hushaysh, east of Sanaa, has risen to 84 casualties: 44 martyrs and 40 wounded,” the Houthis’ ministry of health said, according to the group’s Almasirah TV channel. nigeria.title: SON uploads MANCAP-certified products online to check fakes
nigeria.description: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, has uploaded the list of products certified under its Mandatory Conformity Assessment Programme, MANCAP, to its official website to enable consumers to identify and patronise quality Nigerian-made products. Director-General of SON, Dr Ifeanyi Okeke, disclosed this at the CANEX WKND 2026 held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. Okeke, who was represented by the Director, Corporate Affairs Department, Mrs Talatu Ethan, said the initiative would enable consumers to verify certified products and make informed purchasing decisions. He said: “This development will help consumers find and buy quality products easily. It puts the power of choice in the hands of the Nigerian consumer, and it rewards manufacturers who have done the right thing by meeting our standards.” The SON boss urged members of the public to visit the organisation’s website to verify certified products, while encouraging them to report products bearing fake or questionable certification marks. He explained that SON’s participation at CANEX WKND 2026 was aimed at taking its quality assurance message directly to manufacturers, small business owners and consumers. “Our presence here is about meeting businesses where they are. Many creative and small enterprises have excellent products but do not know how to get them certified. Certification opens doors to bigger markets, here at home and across Africa, and it protects the consumer,” he said. At its exhibition stand, SON officials engaged exhibitors and visitors on product certification under the Nigerian Industrial Standards, NIS. They also educated participants on MANCAP, which covers locally manufactured products, and the SON Conformity Assessment Programme, SONCAP, applicable to imported products. Visitors were also sensitised on how to identify substandard and counterfeit products, verify the SON authentication mark and report suspicious goods. Small and medium-sized enterprises, SMEs, received guidance on the certification process, including application, product testing and eventual approval. Okeke stressed that locally manufactured products must meet international standards to compete effectively in global markets, particularly under the Federal Government’s Nigeria First policy. nigeria.description: By Yinka Kolawole A Nigerian woman entrepreneur, Biobele Oyibo, has won the Technology Award at the 2026 Empretec Women in Business Awards held during the 9th World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar. Oyibo, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Earlybean, was recognised for leveraging technology to promote financial literacy and inclusion among young people. The awards organised under the theme, “Women-led businesses and the art of scale”, celebrated women entrepreneurs driving innovation, sustainability and business growth across four categories: Leadership, Sustainability, Innovation and Technology. The event brought together entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and business leaders to celebrate the winners and connect them with funding, markets, expertise and networks to expand their businesses. The awards highlighted the role of women-led enterprises in creating jobs, deploying new technologies and addressing economic, social and environmental challenges. Other winners included Sandra Letio of Uganda, who received the Leadership Award for building an agribusiness that works with more than 5,000 smallholder farmers; and Paula Gianserra of Argentina, winner of the Sustainability Award for advancing forest restoration through artificial intelligence, biotechnology and drone seeding. The Innovation Award went to Aisha Albinali of Qatar, Co-Founder of Wafir, for transforming traditional savings practices into a financial technology solution, and Adriana Fernandes of Brazil, Chief Executive Officer of Mátrika Special Foods, for improving access to safe, quality food for people with allergies and dietary restrictions. The team won their first FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. Officials of the Nigeria Football Federation and some supporters received the victorious Flamingos, who landed in the early hours of the day, at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja. The triumph is another landmark for a team that had already established itself as one of Africa’s leading sides at the age-grade level. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. nigeria.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has urged manufacturers to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced technologies and energy-efficient solutions to tackle rising production costs, strengthen energy security and improve industrial competitiveness. He noted that AI and smart manufacturing systems could help industries optimise energy use, minimise production losses, lower operating costs and improve product quality, particularly amid persistent electricity supply challenges. nigeria.title: Power outages, rising costs slow manufacturing growth —NESG
nigeria.description: By Yinka Kolawole Frequent power outages, rising production costs and limited access to credit are slowing manufacturing growth in Nigeria, with businesses struggling to sustain operations amid persistent infrastructure challenges, the October 2026 Business Confidence Monitor (BCM) by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) has shown. The report indicated that manufacturing remained in expansion territory in October, but its Current Business Performance Index declined to 107.3 points from 108.4 points in September and 111.3 points in October 2025, reflecting a moderation in business activity. It identified incessant power outages, inadequate raw material supplies, high rental costs, limited access to credit and infrastructure deficiencies as major constraints confronting manufacturers during the month. According to NESG, these challenges continued to amplify operating costs, despite sustained expansion in business activities across the economy. The impact was particularly evident in key manufacturing subsectors. Textile, Apparel and Footwear slipped into contraction territory, with its performance index plunging to 99.7 points in October from 127.5 points in September. Cement also remained in contraction at 94.5 points, while Food, Beverage and Tobacco was the only one of the three major manufacturing subsectors to record improved performance and remain in expansion territory. The report’s findings underscore the growing burden of unreliable electricity on manufacturers, who depend on stable power supply to sustain production lines, process raw materials and maintain factory operations. Frequent outages force businesses to rely on alternative energy sources, adding to production costs and weakening their competitiveness. At the broader economy level, Nigeria’s Current Business Performance Index moderated to 115.4 points in October from 117.8 points in September, although it remained above the 111.3 points recorded in October 2025. All sectors remained in expansion territory, but only Trade and Services recorded improved performance compared with the preceding month. Agriculture, Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing experienced slower growth. The cost pressures were also reflected in the NESG’s business indicators. The cost of doing business sub-index stood at 45.2 points in October, while the prices sub-index was 65.5 points, both significantly below the 100-point neutral threshold, indicating that most firms continued to face elevated operating costs and producer prices. Despite the challenges, the Future Business Expectations Index rose to 130.8 points in October from 128.9 points in September, signalling improved optimism about business conditions over the next one to three months. nigeria.title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams
nigeria.description: The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information. The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs. The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X, (formerly known as Twitter) amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack. ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications. “When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said. Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information. “Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added. Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests. Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is one of the winningest active coaches in the NFL, but his status as a quarterback whisperer is being called into question. At one point, O'Connell was considered a bright young head coach who would get the most out of any quarterback on his team. Over time, though, the Vikings still haven't solved their quarterback issues, while Minnesota's former signal-callers have thrived elsewhere. Now, with Kyler Murray the latest Vikings quarterback who isn't playing up to expectations, O'Connell's status as a quarterback guru has waned. The Vikings head coach needs to turn that around for Minnesota to compete for a Super Bowl. Here's a breakdown of every quarterback to start a game with the Vikings under O'Connell. MORE : Who needs Jonathan Taylor the most? Vikings QB timeline under Kevin O'Connell Kirk Cousins (2022-23) O'Connell inherited Cousins when he first arrived in Minnesota in 2022, and the two were a great pair. Cousins started every game for the Vikings that year, leading Minnesota to the playoffs with a 13-4 record while totaling 4,547 passing yards and 29 passing touchdowns. That season continued Cousins' strong play for the Vikings, as his numbers were similar to his seasonal production since signing with Minnesota in 2018. From a wins standpoint, though, Cousins had only won double-digit games once before and had never won more than 10 contests. In 2023, Cousins had a solid start before he tore his Achilles, which was a huge blow ahead of free agency. In 25 games with O'Connell, Cousins produced 275.12 passing yards per game with 37 passing touchdowns in total. While the Cardinals had just one win up to that point, Dobbs had 14 total touchdowns, passing and rushing, and showed enough to get a chance elsewhere. Dobbs' production slightly dipped when he began playing for the Vikings, and he was unable to fill Cousins' shoes. Dobbs started four games for Minnesota, appearing in five total contests, and had just 179 passing yards per game. sports.title: 4 winners and losers from the Patriots’ loss to the Packers
sports.description: The New England Patriots were largely uncompetitive in a 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. They have now dropped to 5-4 on the season. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Week 9 contest. Winners N/A Losers CB Christian Gonzalez: The Patriots’ top corner was not his usual self on Sunday. Gonzalez was on scene for several explosive plays and took fault for a miscommunication that resulted in Matthew Golden’s 5-yard touchdown. Both Golden and Christian Watson posted 80-plus yards with Gonzalez in coverage while he surrendered 187 yards on a career-high 10 receptions in total. New England’s secondary is too talented to be playing at this level in recent weeks, and that begins with Gonzalez. QB Drake Maye: There were positive moments for Maye against Green Bay, but the quarterback ultimately struggled throwing three first-half interceptions that led to an early deficit. Maye’s interceptions came when he pushed the ball down the field, which was a concern entering the week against a zone heavy Packers defense that led the league in takeaways. Offensive line: Behind their fifth different starting combination, the pressure got to Maye early on Sunday. The Packers’ pressure schemes gave New England’s front fits as Maye was sacked four times and was forced into four throwaways. In total, Maye was under pressure on over 50% of his drop backs. RG Matt Pryor was initially charted with four pressures to lead the group. Injuries: As they have all season, the injuries continued to pile up. The Patriots lost CB Carlton Davis (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee), ST Brenden Schooler (hamstring), and RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) in the loss. They did get positive news with starting left tackle Will Campbell, who would have returned in a closer game, but the roster is beaten down ahead of a trip to Germany — which could alter recovery timelines as the team departs Wednesday evening. Honorable mentions DeMario Douglas recorded his second career 100-yard game behind a beautifully-ran 36-yard corner-post route. Mack Hollins finished with three catches and a touchdown in his return. Efton Chism also found the end zone and had five catches. It was a down day for Kyle Williams, who failed to haul in a deep ball and was targeted on Maye’s second interception (which was on the quarterback). Rhamondre Stevenson’s fumble was the Patriots fourth turnover of the day. They now have a -11 turnover differential on the season. Milton Williams flashed throughout the day with three pressures and a TFL in the run game. Rookie cornerback Karon Prunty replaced an injured Carlton Davis at corner. While Prunty had an impressive gunner rep to help down a punt, the Packers immediately picked on him defensively. Packers were 4-of-5 in the red zone. The Patriots kickoff coverage continues to be shaky as they allowed a 48-yard return. Punter Mitch Wishnowsky continues to punt well and recorded four i20s.

sports.description: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula. © IMAGN The All-American 2026 WTA Finals Group 1 match between Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula lasted two hours and 39 minutes on Sunday in Indian Wells. This was also why Pegula looked pretty exhausted in the third set. “It’s tough when a match gets really physical against Coco; to be honest, it’s probably not in my favor,” Pegula told reporters as seen in Christian Court’s X. “I think the first two sets especially were super physical, and I just had a little lull at the beginning of the third, which was unfortunate, like that first game… I thought her movement, I mean, I say this every time, but is the best on tour. technology.title: Memory crunch makes refurbished kit look a lot less secondhand
technology.description: Rising memory prices are pushing more customers toward refurbished tech, suppliers say, with warranties of up to three years helping to make secondhand kit a less daunting purchase. Memory costs have more than quadrupled this year as manufacturers prioritize more lucrative high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for servers powering AI datacenters. Many enterprises are keeping equipment longer in an uncertain economy. Ben Caddy, senior analyst at Omdia, said suppliers were linking refresh discussions with opportunities to recover value from customers' aging kit. By 2030, he predicted, 35 percent of "all the hardware sold for the channel will be taken back by partners," driven "by the sheer economic logic of taking equipment back, recovering value, and embracing more circular IT lifecycles." This is already helping some customers "unlock some capital to put towards those [relatively] small refresh plans," he said while hosting a panel on circular IT at last month's Canalys Forums in Barcelona. Refurbished smartphones are growing in popularity, but persuading customers to trade in their old devices remains a constraint on supply. The same applies to PCs and other equipment, said Jon Sansom, MD at GreenSafe IT. "Availability is a challenge," he said. Marcel Joosten, group director of marketing and digital commerce at tech lifecycle specialist XTENTEC, said the company now offers trade-ins when customers buy new kit. "We're actually financing the residual value" at the end of year two, three, or four, when customers return the equipment, he told the audience. XTENTEC collects, refurbishes, rents, and resells equipment, and has an agreement with HP to renovate aging products, with a two or even three-year warranty available as "just an SKU on the list from HP." Joosten said equivalent support, including HP Care Pack services, helped make refurbished equipment more attractive to buyers. Customers want to cut their carbon footprint, and many public and private sector tenders require it. But the "most important thing" for many is trust, said Patrick Molberg, CEO of Advania Finance. "The customers have to trust the refurbished equipment and have to trust the process. And I think one of the things that we have to be better at as a whole is that we kind of need to have a standard methodology regarding verification." Work on verification standards with vendors including HP, Lenovo, and Dell is ongoing, Molberg said. He also argued that lifecycle services should be built into purchasing decisions rather than added three or four years later. Joosten argued that listed US tech companies' focus on quarterly sales and market share can work against refurbishment. "That needs to change," he said. "I think there should be a market share figure for circularity." ®

This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Oriel" who told us he once worked for a vendor of small business accounting software. This story comes from a time when software shipped on CD-ROMs and users bought it off the shelf in actual shops. The vendor released a new version each year and always shipped it before a major holiday that's celebrated with a giant meal. Oriel was part of the team whose job it was to get the package ready on time. In the previous year, they flubbed the job because the program didn't always install itself on some PCs running Windows 95 or Windows ME machines system due to registry corruption. What went wrong was that not long after the software was shipped, the vendor's support lines started getting calls from customers who complained that after installing the accounting package none of their other software would work. The company decided the best thing to do was to tell affected customers they should go and buy a new PC – and that it would pick up the bill, no questions asked. technology.title: Linus Torvalds sees signs AI-prompted patch flood has peaked
technology.description: The worst of the patchpocalypse may be behind us, according to Linus Torvalds. Writing in his weekly kernel update post , the Linux kernel dev leader delivered Linux 7.4 rc2 – the second rough cut of the next kernel – which he rated as a big release for two reasons. One is that he left some code out of rc1, because he was busy and because it was already the largest such release in the history of the kernel. The other is what Torvalds described as “various AI fixes.” Such fixes are necessary because ever since Anthropic launched its Mythos bug-finding model in April , developers have been able to find more software flaws than was previously possible. Microsoft, for example, addressed a record 974 flaws in September – its third record fixing spree this year after it whacked 622 flaws in July and 206 in June. Oracle addressed 1,449 flaws in a single month. That’s many more patches than IT teams are set up to handle, yet they must find ways to deal with bugs more quickly because attackers are increasingly targeting flaws found by AI . Torvalds’ post suggests that, perhaps, the worst of this is behind us. “This time around Alexei claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true,” he wrote. That’s a reference to Alexei Starovoitov, co-creator and lead dev on the Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), the project that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs within the Linux kernel. “I think most other areas haven't reached that point yet, but it's at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn,” he added. “Don't hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we'll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.” If Torvalds is correct, that’s welcome news. The Linux kernel’s 40-million-plus lines of code makes it one of the world’s bigger software projects. If AI soon stops finding flaws in other parts of the kernel beyond eBPF, perhaps the deluge of fixes developers and users alike will need to handle has peaked. ®

The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula’s shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch’s head. Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation . What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to — because it has been partly eroded by — the nearby star Rigel . One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image . The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel’s intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth’s daytime sky to appear blue , although the scatterers in planet Earth’s atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen . NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin This story is an update to the Antarctic ozone hole feature in our World of Change series , which documents how Earth changes over months, seasons, and years. The stratospheric ozone layer protects life on Earth by absorbing ultraviolet light, which damages DNA in plants and animals (including humans) and leads to sunburns and skin cancer. Prior to 1979, scientists had not observed atmospheric ozone concentrations below 220 Dobson Units . But in 1985, British Antarctic Survey scientists using ground-based measurements at Halley Research Station reported that Earth’s natural sunscreen was thinning dramatically over Antarctica each spring. NASA satellite instruments revealed the continental scale of this Antarctic ozone thinning, and it came to be known as the ozone hole. The data visualizations below shows the ozone hole each year from 1979 through 2026 (no data are available for 1995). The measurements were made from 1979-2004 by the TOMS (NASA’s Total Ozone Mapping Spectrometer) instruments on Nimbus-7 and several additional satellites; from 2005-2011 by the OMI (Ozone Monitoring Instrument) on the Aura satellite; from 2012-2025 by the OMPS (Ozone Mapping and Profiler Suite) on the Suomi NPP satellite; and in 2026 by the OMPS on the NOAA-20 satellite. Red and yellow areas indicate the ozone hole. As the images show, the word hole isn’t literal; no place is empty of ozone. Scientists use the word hole as a metaphor for the area in which ozone concentrations drop below the historical threshold of 220 Dobson Units . science.title: Legendary sci-fi magazine 'Starlog' returns as a yearly release, just in time for its 50th anniversary
science.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Kerry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year. I don't think we're going to get back to where we were with Apollo, but once a year is the minimum … I would testify that to Congress in this role years down the road. "If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. "That's what we're doing with Artemis III, and that's what's going to better prepare us for Artemis IV." A new space race So, how is NASA coping with the challenges that face them as they approach Artemis III ahead of a crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV, which is targeted for 2028? While NASA can learn some lessons from past moon missions with Apollo, today it's primarily relying on the extensive experience and talent within the agency, according to Isaacman.
